page: Amazon Web Services x8g.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 32 dedicated physical cores built on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V2 model running at 2.8 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor, does not include local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight the server's memory subsystem performance, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 390.87 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 175.81 GB/sec, both placing in the top tier. The Passmark memory score and database operations benchmarks also rank in the top tier, with database operations scoring 46,855.81. Multi-core performance is strong, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,432.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 118.88 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,866.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1,707.09.

The x8g.8xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads due to its high resource density and the power-efficient Arm-based Graviton architecture. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff. The instance is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, including large-memory databases, Redis caching layers (achieving 66.43 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks), and high-throughput static web serving. It is less suited for large-scale LLM text generation, where performance falls into the weak to average categories.
